articles.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 3.8 Live Audio: real‑time voice LLM over WebSocket
articles.dek: A new Gemini endpoint streams microphone audio to the model and returns spoken replies, cutting per‑hour costs to a fraction of competing services.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Google launched Gemini 3.8 Live Audio on Sep 15 2026, exposing a WebSocket‑based streaming endpoint that feeds raw microphone audio into the Gemini LLM and returns spoken responses in near‑real‑time [FACT:821165a955bad4c3a61cb0a800da548d][FACT:789e9e79130f493d624a7a6ff4fd568e]. Builders can now add turn‑by‑turn voice interaction to any web app without a custom speech pipeline, and the per‑hour pricing is about ten‑times cheaper than comparable GPT‑Live offerings [FACT:e9a27b1f01a48826a930bdb9b6ad0ac2].
Why This Matters

The cheap, low‑latency audio channel removes the biggest friction point for conversational agents—stitching speech‑to‑text and text‑to‑speech together—so you can focus on prompting and business logic [FACT:2ce027dc92dc804bfcdab3680c7dd92e]. Early testers report smooth multi‑step dialogues, meaning you can build richer conversations without extra orchestration [FACT:2ce027dc92dc804bfcdab3680c7dd92e].
What Happened

Google’s DeepMind team announced the feature in a brief blog post and opened a public “getting‑started” tutorial that walks you through creating a WebSocket, piping the browser’s Web Audio API into it, and handling the streamed audio reply [FACT:e8af5dfcfb5db9e0dcc566c250209869][FACT:2f5169a05402772fa8993df12719e0bc]. The same announcement was covered by The Decoder, confirming the rollout and cost claims [FACT:17031654ad0a6e3c6cdd36a790de58d9].
Builder View

The endpoint lives at wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-live:streamAudio [FACT:789e9e79130f493d624a7a6ff4fd568e] and expects a binary Opus‑encoded stream; the client side can use the native Web Audio API’s MediaStreamAudioSourceNode to feed microphone data directly [FACT:1ea6792aa09ac8f708d73ddb4e6216cc]. Because the service accepts multi‑step requests—e.g., “ask a follow‑up after the first answer”—you can keep the conversation on a single socket without extra round‑trips [FACT:2ce027dc92dc804bfcdab3680c7dd92e].
Open Questions

Google has only quoted “sub‑second” latency; real‑world benchmarks are still missing. The rollout is currently limited to US‑based accounts, and finer‑grained pricing tiers beyond the advertised hourly rate have not been disclosed [FACT:e9a27b1f01a48826a930bdb9b6ad0ac2].
Ardur Take

Given the cost advantage, the ready‑made WebSocket recipe, and early positive feedback, it’s worth spinning up a prototype this week if voice is in your product roadmap. Gemini Live Audio currently offers the cheapest production‑grade voice‑LLM integration on the market [FACT:e9a27b1f01a48826a930bdb9b6ad0ac2][FACT:821165a955bad4c3a61cb0a800da548d].

articles.headline: containerd 2.4.0‑rc.0 lands with static & Ubuntu builds plus API 1.12.0‑rc.1
articles.dek: A pre‑release of containerd 2.4.0‑rc.0 ships both a statically linked tarball and a glibc‑linked Ubuntu tarball, and updates the API to 1.12.0‑rc.1.

body.text: Key Takeaway

containerd 2.4.0‑rc.0 arrives as a pre‑release and includes two binaries – a static build ([FACT:c4925f532a5a91e5cbb9ec5afb454486]) and a glibc‑linked Ubuntu build ([FACT:d1806fd7f70fc291b5365cdbb37a5740]) – plus API version 1.12.0‑rc.1 ([FACT:478eb5ceb03ded47319cdf0ee2363d9f]) ([FACT:c03e7697304f052e8067d8046a3cb547]).
Why This Matters

If your worker nodes run Ubuntu, you can use the glibc‑linked package directly; if you need a self‑contained binary for a stripped‑down OS, the static tarball fits the bill. Choosing the right binary now avoids a later migration when the GA drops ([FACT:c4925f532a5a91e5cbb9ec5afb454486]; [FACT:d1806fd7f70fc291b5365cdbb37a5740]).
What Happened

The release notes list the two tarballs under the arch directory and label them the recommended downloads for the 2.4 series ([FACT:5729679e327103f66dab9bd430931bf4]). This is the first time containerd publishes a static tarball alongside the traditional dynamic Ubuntu package for the same version ([FACT:c4925f532a5a91e5cbb9ec5afb454486]; [FACT:d1806fd7f70fc291b5365cdbb37a5740]).
Builder View

Download the tarball that matches your node OS, verify the SHA256 checksum, extract to /opt/containerd, and point your systemd unit to the new binary. The static binary works on any glibc‑based distro, while the Ubuntu tarball assumes the host’s glibc version matches Ubuntu’s runtime ([FACT:d1806fd7f70fc291b5365cdbb37a5740]; [FACT:c4925f532a5a91e5cbb9ec5afb454486]).
Open Questions

Because this is still a pre‑release, performance numbers, the exact GA timeline, and whether the static package will later include optional snapshotter plugins have not been published ([FACT:c03e7697304f052e8067d8046a3cb547]).
Ardur Take

For clusters that can tolerate a pre‑release, grab the matching tarball now and run a small upgrade test on a staging node. Teams that prioritize a stable support lifecycle should stick with the current GA version until containerd 2.4.0 is officially released ([FACT:887110a12d1d5f35e007c26b1c01221f]).
